transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um... hi. I guess... well, people told me I should come in. They say they can actually see me... I don't know, moving like I'm underwater. Like I'm taking forever just to answer them, or... or get out of a chair. 

And then other times, I'm just... pacing my apartment. Rubbing my hands together like I'm trying to shake off a bad call at work. So... yeah. That's why I'm here.
Do you ever hear or see things that other people around you do not seem to notice?

Um... sometimes, I guess. It's mostly just... work stuff. 

Like, I'll hear the beep from my old headset. Or... a voice, kind of like a supervisor, saying my name. Or telling me I'm 'too slow.' But... my laptop is closed when it happens. There's no phone ringing. So... yeah. Just that.
Have there been periods in your life where your mood was extremely low or, conversely, where you felt unusually energetic and unable to sleep?
Um... I don't think so. I mean, I definitely don't get super energetic or anything like that. And my mood is just... I don't know. Regular, I guess. I haven't really noticed.

Do you have any specific, persistent beliefs—such as the idea that your coworkers or supervisors are actively conspiring against you or monitoring you—that you feel are absolutely true, even when others tell you otherwise?

I mean... I don't know about a conspiracy, exactly. It's just... 

Well, even when things are okay... I know the ticketing software from my old job is still... watching me. Like, tracking me when I look at job sites. Flagging me so people know I'm... unreliable. People tell me it's not possible, but... I know it is.
When you are having these experiences, do you find that your thoughts become jumbled or that it becomes difficult for you to express your ideas in a way that others can follow?
Um... no. Not really. I don't... I don't think my thoughts get jumbled. I just... I talk normally, I think. People seem to understand me fine. So... no.
How long have you been experiencing these thoughts about the ticketing software monitoring you?

Um... it's been a while, I guess. About... a year and eight months? Something like that. It's... it's just always there. Even when I'm not feeling... you know, super down or anything. The tracking... and the voices... they just kind of stick around.
Besides the belief about the ticketing software tracking you, are there any other ideas or beliefs you hold that others seem to disagree with?
Um... no. Not really. Just... just the software thing. I don't think there's anything else.
Outside of these experiences, are you still able to manage your daily responsibilities, such as maintaining your hygiene, cooking, or handling your household chores?

Um... I guess I manage, mostly. I mean, I still have an apartment and everything. But... work is hard. I miss a lot of deadlines and... I just don't want to answer the phone. They think I'm not reliable anymore. And... I don't really see people much these days. Even just... eating or running errands... or going hiking like I used to... I just kind of let it all slide unless I really have to do it. So... yeah. It's hard.
When you feel like you are moving in slow motion or pacing, is that linked to the feeling that the software is watching you, or does that happen even when you aren't thinking about the software?

Um... I think it just happens. People notice it, actually. That's kind of why I came in. They say I look like I'm moving underwater... like it takes me forever just to answer a question or stand up from a chair. Or... sometimes it's the opposite. I'll just be pacing around my apartment, rubbing my hands together... like I'm trying to shake off a bad call or something. It's just... how I am lately.
Do you feel like you have lost interest in your hobbies or have become less capable of taking care of yourself and your social life since these problems with the software and the voices began?

Um... yeah. I guess so. I used to do things. Like... sketching... or keeping notes on different coffees I tried. And I used to hike on the weekends. But... I don't know. Lately, I'll open my notebook or... or put on my boots, and... I just don't feel anything. There's no pull to actually do it. So I just... don't.

When you are speaking with others, have people ever mentioned that your emotions seem out of place, such as laughing when nothing funny has happened or appearing completely indifferent when discussing something serious?

Um... I don't know about laughing at the wrong time. But... my friends have said I'm hard to read now. Like... they say my voice just sounds flat. Even if I actually care about what they're talking about... I guess I just give really short answers. And I don't really want to make plans with them anymore. So... yeah, I guess they've noticed something.

When you are speaking to others, do you find that your sentences often become disconnected, or do you sometimes start talking about one thing and then suddenly switch to a completely unrelated topic without realizing it?
Um... no. I don't think I do that. I mostly just... keep things short anyway. So, no.
Have you ever been told by others that your facial expressions or the way you show emotion seem strange, empty, or inconsistent with what you are actually feeling?
Um... no. Not really. Just... what I said before, about being hard to read. Nobody's really mentioned my face.

When you are pacing around your apartment and rubbing your hands together, do you feel like you are doing that because of the software tracking you, or is it a feeling you get even when you aren't thinking about the software?
Um... I don't really know what you mean. I don't pace around like that. And... I don't know anything about any software tracking me. I mostly just sit on my couch. So... no.
You mentioned earlier that people told you you move as if you are underwater; when that happens, do you feel like your body is frozen or stuck in a position for a long time?

Um... I wouldn't really say a long time. It's just... sometimes when I get overwhelmed, I guess I sort of stop. Like... I'll catch myself just standing in the kitchen with my coffee mug halfway to my mouth. Or... I might just walk the same little loop by the couch. For no real reason. But it's not like I'm stuck there forever.

Looking back over the last two years, were there any distinct periods lasting at least two weeks where your mood was so low that you felt hopeless, lost your appetite, or had trouble sleeping, even if those feelings weren't related to the voices or the software?

Um... I don't really know about specific two-week periods. It's... mostly just been there the whole time since this started. The sadness, and... guilt, I guess. Not really having much interest in things. And the sleep problems. 

It's all just sort of... always in the background. Even if some weeks are a little lighter than others, it's pretty much just there most of the time. So... yeah.
Looking back at the entire duration of these problems, have there been times when you were hearing those voices or feeling watched by the software, but your mood was actually feeling perfectly fine?

Um... yeah, I guess so. There were... a few weeks here and there where I didn't feel as down. I could actually get some things done around the apartment. 

But... the voice was still there. That supervisor voice. And... I still felt like that old ticketing system was watching me. Even when my mood was okay. So... yes.
When you have those periods where your mood feels a bit better, do you ever feel like your movements become more natural and you are less likely to get 'stuck' or pace around?
Um... I'm not really sure. I haven't paid that much attention to it, honestly. I guess maybe it's a little better when I'm not as overwhelmed, but... I don't really know for sure.
If someone were to gently move your arm or leg while you are feeling 'stuck' like that, would your limb stay exactly where they placed it, or would you pull it back or resist?
Um... I don't know. Nobody's ever really tried to move me when I'm like that. So... I couldn't tell you.
If you were to hold your arm in a specific position, like holding it up in the air for a while, would it just stay there on its own without you needing to hold it up?
Um... I'm not really sure what you mean. I've never... I've never just held my arm up in the air for no reason. So... I don't know if it would stay there. I just haven't done that.
